definitions.explanation: A disease or condition for which there is no known cure. A literary and somewhat formal expression.

examples.japanese: {不治|ふじ}の{病|やまい}にかかった。
examples.english: He fell ill with an incurable disease.

examples.japanese: かつて{不治|ふじ}の{病|やまい}とされていた{病気|びょうき}も、{今|いま}は{治療法|ちりょうほう}がある。
examples.english: Diseases once considered incurable now have treatments.

examples.japanese: {不治|ふじ}の{病|やまい}を{宣告|せんこく}された{彼|かれ}は、{残|のこ}りの{人生|じんせい}を{大切|たいせつ}に{生|い}きようと{決意|けつい}した。
examples.english: Diagnosed with a terminal illness, he resolved to live the rest of his life to the fullest.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary and somewhat formal expression. In medical contexts, {難病|なんびょう} (intractable disease) is the more technical term. {不治|ふじ}の{病|やまい} carries dramatic weight and appears frequently in literature, drama, and news stories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不治|ふじ}の{病|やまい}にかかる (to contract an incurable disease)
- {不治|ふじ}の{病|やまい}を{宣告|せんこく}される (to be diagnosed with a terminal illness)
- {不治|ふじ}の{病|やまい}と{闘|たたか}う (to fight an incurable disease)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {難病|なんびょう}: intractable disease — the medical/administrative term
- {末期|まっき}の{病|やまい}: terminal illness — emphasizes the final stage
